document_title: Four candidates, three answers. No law yet.
post_copy:
Four candidates for Alaska governor gave three answers on data centers. A 20,000-acre land decision may not wait for the winner.

Kreiss-Tomkins wants a "pause." Wilson says "never" to hyperscale. Bronson is "a big believer" and Taylor would "embrace it."

Ranked choice on November 18th, if needed, and certification by November 25th can settle who governs. Neither writes a data center law. The House never took up the bill the Senate passed 14 to 5.

DNR's commissioner calls a Houston decision before noon December 7th "certainly possible." The site could include data centers. AIDEA has maintained they're unlikely.

Two frames hold the candidates' words. One each holds the early count, the DNR hearing, the Pentagon offer, a Fairbanks town hall of about 150 and the Senate vote.

What should a data center law require before DNR decides on Houston?

#AlaskaGovernor #DataCenterPolicy #MatSu

slides.kicker: ALASKA'S GOVERNOR RACE, ON DATA CENTERS
slides.headline: Pause. Never hyperscale. Believer. Embrace.
Four candidates. Three answers.
labels: Backs a moratorium until the Legislature passes a framework.
"I will never allow Alaska to be littered with hyperscale data centers"
"I'm a big believer in data centers."
"I think we need to embrace it."

slides.headline: An early count. Not a result.
slides.body: With 11% of precincts in, Kreiss-Tomkins led with 55%, Wilson 28%, Bronson 11%, Taylor 6%. If nobody tops 50%, ranked choice decides it November 18th.

slides.headline: "It's certainly possible."
slides.body: Under subpoena, DNR's commissioner was asked if the 20,000-acre Houston transfer to AIDEA could be decided before December 7th. The district could include data centers. AIDEA has maintained they're unlikely there.

slides.headline: Up to a dozen. None awarded as of September 15th.
slides.body: The Pentagon wants up to a dozen data centers near Anchorage, Healy and Fairbanks and has offered to lease about 4,700 acres to private companies. Sen. Lisa Murkowski said she is "not a proponent," citing "an insecure energy base."

slides.headline: "Our largest concern is that nobody asked us."
labels: FAIRBANKS DATA CENTER TOWN HALL, OCTOBER 29TH

slides.headline: The Senate passed it 14 to 5. The House never took it up.
slides.body: Even the pause has a condition, a moratorium "until the Legislature can pass a comprehensive regulatory framework." This year a data center bill passed the Senate. The session ended without a House vote.

slides.headline: On the desk at noon, December 7th.
labels: 20,000 acres near Houston to AIDEA. A decision is "certainly possible" before the handoff.
About 4,700 acres offered for lease by the Pentagon. None awarded as of September 15th.
A data center bill passed the Senate 14 to 5. No House vote.

slides.headline: Law first, or land first?
slides.body: Make the case in the comments.

editor_notes_for_email: The vote count is partial. Every number on slide 3 is the early first-round count Alaska Public Media published at 8:51 p.m. November 3rd with 11% of precincts reporting (ADN had 45 of 400 precincts at 8:40 p.m.). The Division of Elections results pages returned 503 during the run, so no newer count was verified. Check the Division of Elections count before posting and consider whether slide 03 needs an update. The slide orders the candidates by position and never by vote share, so a changed count changes only the slide 3 body. AI-company employee contributions in the governor and U.S. Senate races were verified (six Anthropic employees gave Kreiss-Tomkins $372,000 as of the July report, and the Alaska Beacon reports AI-company employee money to Sullivan and Peltola, nearly all of Peltola's from Anthropic employees). They were deliberately kept off the slides and caption, because one flat figure beside a candidate frame implies a link the claims don't support. The studio's production model is made by Anthropic. That's disclosed here for your judgment on whether the post or the sources comment should say so. The Legislature's BASIS site was unreachable (403), so the Senate-passed data center bill appears unnamed and without a bill number. The 14 to 5 vote and the House not taking it up come from the Alaska Beacon's September 21st report. The town hall date of October 29th is inferred from the source's 'Thursday night'. The docket ask box's payload headroom is 5,053 bytes after this run's docket edits, just above the 5,000 byte warn line, so the next few docket additions will cross it.
